deep_analysis.text: Cross-asset signals are mixed rather than confirming a clean regime: gold firmer and VIX sharply lower point to easing risk aversion, yet falling equities momentum, softer BTC, and rising US10Y suggest the dollar retains underlying support. DXY is flat, reflecting this tug-of-war, while the H4 risk-off backdrop sits against a ranging H1 tape. The dominant theme is Fed-BoE policy divergence, with hike-odds repricing keeping the dollar bloc firm against European currencies. Ahead lies a heavy central-bank slate—US CPI/PPI, ECB, BoE, BoC and RBNZ decisions within the next day—setting up a volatile stretch across major and dollar-bloc currencies.

week_ahead.text: This week's dominant theme centers on major economic data releases from Germany, the eurozone, the US, and the UK, alongside central bank decisions , creating conflicting signals between soft US data and hawkish Fed messaging that will drive dollar direction. The Fed's interest rate decision was the past week's key event , and Friday's CPI release will be the most critical catalyst for USD this week, as a higher-than-expected reading could reinforce rate-hike expectations and strengthen the dollar. USD/CAD will depend heavily on whether trade tensions ease through negotiation or intensify further, while improving Canadian economic conditions may support the currency , making this pair particularly sensitive to geopolitical shifts. The biggest wildcard is the divergence between resilient core inflation data and weakening labor markets, which could trigger sharp reversals in dollar positioning if Friday's CPI surprises materially on either side.
